title: Impossible-Differential to Multidimensional-Linear Key Recovery
summary: Practical distinguishers can have similar data costs, but converting chosen-plaintext impossible-differential key recovery into known-plaintext multidimensional-linear key recovery remains open.

formal_statement.body: Practical impossible-differential distinguishers can have data complexity similar to multidimensional-linear distinguishers, but the time and memory complexity of the multidimensional-linear distinguisher can limit such a transformation. Because first-round key recovery modifies the data complexity of truncated- or impossible-differential attacks, determine whether a chosen-plaintext impossible-differential first-round key-recovery attack can be transformed into a known-plaintext multidimensional-linear key-recovery attack while accounting for its data, time, and memory complexity.

scope.domain: Symmetric cryptanalysis of block-cipher key recovery using impossible-differential and multidimensional-linear attacks.
parameters: Plaintext access model — chosen plaintext for the source attack and known plaintext for the target attack
Key-recovery position — recovery in the first round
Data complexity — changes under first-round key recovery and must be accounted for in the transformation
Time and memory complexity — potential limiting costs of the multidimensional-linear attack
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a chosen-plaintext impossible-differential first-round key-recovery attack can be transformed into a known-plaintext multidimensional-linear key-recovery attack while accounting for data, time, and memory complexity.

citations.label: Links between Truncated Differential and Multidimensional Linear Properties of Block Ciphers and Underlying Attack Complexities

progress.summary: The source observes that practical impossible-differential and multidimensional-linear distinguishers can have similar data complexity, while time and memory can limit the transformation. It explicitly leaves the corresponding first-round key-recovery transformation open.
citation_labels: Céline Blondeau et al., Links between Truncated Differential and Multidimensional Linear Properties of Block Ciphers and Underlying Attack Complexities
